key_insight: WC–Co–Cr coating performance depends on powder morphology and spray method: detonation spraying favors hardness, while HVOF yields a dense, uniform coating with low friction.
engineering_relevance: Selecting powder morphology and spraying conditions can improve coating wear resistance and machine-part durability under intensive friction and high loads.
method: Compared detonation-sprayed and HVOF WC–Co–Cr coatings.
Examined powder morphology and coating microstructure using SEM and EDS.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports average microhardness of 1449 HV for detonation spraying and a friction coefficient of Kt = 0.143 for HVOF.
watch_item: The abstract omits test conditions, variability, and quantitative wear rates, limiting direct translation to service performance.
paper_title: INVESTIGATION OF THE FORMATION OF STRUCTURE AND WEAR-RESISTANT PROPERTIES OF WC–CO–CR COATINGS PRODUCED BY HVOF AND DETONATION SPRAYING
